newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Technology stocks dip slightly.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Technology stocks dip slightly.

text.p: Several U.S. technology stocks dropped slightly in after-hours trading after Hewlett-Packard Co announced it was disappointed with order and revenue growth in its second quarter, dealers said Thursday.
"Techs took a hit," said one trader.

Compaq Computer Co fell to 95 from a close of 96-3/4 on the New York Stock Exchange, while Gateway 2000 Inc slipped to 68 from 68-7/8 on the Nasdaq. Dell Computer Corp was down to 94-7/8 against 96-1/4 and Intel Corp was at 157 from 158-1/8.
It reported second-quarter earnings of $0.75 a share on revenues of $10.3 billion against $0.69 on $9.9 billion for the same period a year ago.
Staples Inc, which also released results, was trading at 21-1/2 compared to a close of 21-5/8. It had a first-quarter profit of $0.05 a share after charges against $0.08 the previous year.
"It's still not that active," said another dealer. "People are looking (to trade) but they're not going crazy."
Hewlett-Packard's stock was later allowed to resume trading but no deals had been immediately reported, according to a third trader.
The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that session one had a volume of 14,800 shares against 6,200 the previous day. Session two had 983,209 compared to 6.2 million, it added.
